target_customer: Fast growing retail, ecommerce and omnichannel brands and modern manufacturers that outgrow spreadsheets or rigid ERP suites
problem: Legacy ERPs such as NetSuite and SAP are slow to implement and hard to customize, while point solutions do not talk to each other. Tailor offers a headless, API first ERP backend.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform with implementation and enterprise contracts (pricing not published)

founders.name: Yo Shibata
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Misato Takahashi
previous_startups: Speee (co-founded, listed on the TSE in 2020)
founders.background_notes: Per YC company page. TechCrunch 2022 says the founders sold Spotlight to Rakuten for $20 million in 2013.

investors: JPS Growth Investment LP (Japan Post Investment)

competitors.name: Oracle NetSuite
competitors.what: Cloud ERP suite named as the legacy comparison
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent, per TechCrunch hard to customize

technical_complexity.rationale: An ERP backend with GraphQL APIs, workflow state machines and many integrations is a large engineering scope for a small team, though the founders had prior engineering exits.

defensibility.rationale: Once an ERP runs a retailer's operations, switching costs are high. Early on there was one customer and 10 employees (TechCrunch, September 2022), so the moat was prospective.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source seen showing an incumbent copying Tailor or buying it through 2026; Tailor remained independent and raised a Series A in 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (September 2022) reported that Japanese enterprises faced high maintenance costs and slow development, and the company claimed about 70 percent of Japan's software spending goes to custom builds. Legacy ERPs were described as built for the largest organizations.

branding.domain_note: tailor.tech, not an exact .com; a separate company, Tailor Brands, uses a similar name in logo making

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, built around the tailored theme, for example 'Tailored to you, live in weeks'

branding.brand_signature: The 'tailored' theme in the headline and copy, plus being the first Japan based company in YC
branding.community_and_virality: Being described as the first Japan based YC company was picked up by TechCrunch and Taiwanese outlet Bnext in 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a common word shared with other companies and no brand specific press, merch or community was found. The first Japan based YC angle gave press but is not the name.

outcome_analysis: Tailor is active and grew from 10 employees in 2022 to about 40 on the YC page, with a US launch in 2023 and a Series A in 2025 that the company puts at $37 million total. It benefited from serial founders with retail tech exits and from incumbent ERPs described as rigid. No shutdown, acquisition or layoffs were found. Revenue and customer counts are not public.
notes: Series A closed in stages: first close of $14M announced 2025-05-20, expanded to $22M on 2025-07-01, final close announced 2025-11-20 bringing the Series A to $37M (company blog, also Crowdfund Insider). Recorded as one round at the company stated total. Aggregators disagree on totals (ZoomInfo $41.3M raised, CB Insights $41.8M, VCBacked $15.0M, another source $30.7M). The seed was reported by TechCrunch on 2022-09-05. Lead investor of the Series A is not stated by the company; Pulse2 credits ANRI for the first close. Founder education not found. Competitor list is from TechCrunch dated three months after the batch start.
